conventions.convention: The observation count is n ≥ 1; observations and target are real and square-integrable on one probability space. Σ = Cov(Z,Z), c₀ = Cov(Z,Y), and v₀ = Var(Y). Simple prediction uses the known means m and m₀.
Universal trend coefficients range over all of ℝᵠ, q ≥ 1. Unbiasedness for every coefficient vector is Pᵀλ = p₀. Ordinary kriging takes P = 1ₙ and p₀ = 1.

The augmented system uses Σλ + Pν = c₀, so its prediction-error formula is v₀ − λᵀc₀ − νᵀp₀. Its asserted invertibility and coefficient uniqueness require positive-definite Σ and full column rank of P.

Gaussian finite coordinate laws may be singular, but the conditional-mean theorem requires positive-definite observation covariance. AC is assumed, and conditional-expectation equality means almost-sure equality given σ(Z).

The covariance claims use fixed oracle means and covariances. No plug-in guarantee or variogram-system invertibility is asserted; the cited intrinsic-variogram result is invoked for fields indexed by all of ℝᵈ.

load_bearing.statement: Simple prediction is m₀ + λᵀ(Z − m). Ordinary prediction is λᵀZ with 1ₙᵀλ = 1. Universal prediction is λᵀZ with Pᵀλ = p₀ for unrestricted trend coefficients β ∈ ℝᵠ.

For positive-definite Σ, the unique simple mean-square minimizing weights are Σ⁻¹c₀, with error v₀ − c₀ᵀΣ⁻¹c₀. Universal unbiasedness for every β is equivalent to Pᵀλ = p₀. With positive-definite Σ and full-column-rank P, the augmented matrix is invertible, its solution gives the unique unbiased minimizing weights and multiplier, and the error is v₀ − λᵀc₀ − νᵀp₀.

seams_checked.note: Compared the supplying page and Gaussian-block lemma with the consuming Gaussian proof. The lemma requires AC and finite jointly Gaussian blocks with zero cross-covariance, permits singular covariance, and supplies exactly the residual independence used. Kriging adds positive-definiteness only for its observation inverse; it does not attribute that restriction to the independence lemma.

Compared the supplying page, random-field definition, and complete intrinsic-variogram proof with the consuming definition and Remark. The consumer explicitly imposes finite second moments on the considered coordinate vector and preserves the variogram theorem's all-ℝᵈ domain and real zero-sum non-strict inequality. It makes no inference of augmented-system invertibility from conditional negative definiteness.
